results.reasoning: Pass, judged independently of the builder against the checkspace's expenses blueprint and its app with sign-in, served by an unrecorded Playwright harness on ports 4713 (walkdown), 4725 (panel host), 4749 and 4750 (the app); nothing was driven through 4700 except reading the designs and as-built pages. Every then step held. As the org manager the app's log reads POST /dev/session with user_id 31, GET /expenses/7, GET /expenses/11, in that order, and the frame ends on Expense 11 as 31. detail.signed-in reads 'Signing in as View-only org manager, a Manager.' while the POST is held and 'Signed in as ...' once the screen's own step is the one running; the list is headed 'View-only org manager signs in' then 'Then this screen's own steps', numbered 1 to 3. As the persona alone the first user signs in (user_id 14, Expense 8). As Visitor, in a fresh tab, only GET /expenses/9 is asked, uid null, and the line reads 'Nobody signs in as Visitor. No sign-in runs.' The locked-out user stops at step 2 of 2 with /expenses/501 never asked, and panel.setup-failed reads 'Sign-in stopped at step 2 of 2', a Whose row 'Signing in as Locked-out manager', and 'This was a step of signing in as Locked-out manager, not one of this screen's own.' The prose screen runs the one POST, loads /expenses/10 and shows the prose under 'This screen's own setup, shown and not run'. Copy matched the three designs verbatim in every state compared: the line, both headings, the card's whose line and prose note, and the failed card for a status, a wait that never lands and a missing fixture (the last two on fixtures the harness added to the throwaway copy: a staging target with a base URL and a user whose wait_for never lands). Run setup again repeats the sign-in after a pass and after a failure; a second rule on the same screen signs in once; the review target posts its own fixture (77). Redlines met and true: the as-built is drawn over the example with a returning visitor given to the payload; 'Signs in as' before a run and after a failed sign-in; only the failed status is drawn. Edges found, none a step of the rule, weighed and reported to the dispatching agent rather than filed. (1) About 50%, for any blueprint with a no-users persona on an app with sessions: the Visitor screen opened after a manager screen in the same tab shows the app still signed in as 14 beside 'Nobody signs in as Visitor'; the words are true and the page is not a visitor's. (2) About 40%: with the user's fixture set and the path's fixture missing, nothing runs and the card says 'Setup did not run', yet the line reads 'Signed in as View-only org manager'. (3) About 25%: going to an as: screen with no steps does not leave the setup before it, so after a failed sign-in the Visitor rule keeps the Locked-out manager's failure card over its own loaded page, Run setup again does not clear it, and leaving a sign-in mid-run for the Visitor rule ends with the frame on /expenses/7 under a rule that says /expenses/9. Under 10%, named only: a window 560px wide or less clips the card or lays it over the sidebar, which is the cover's own behaviour from before this slice; a user whose setup is prose reads 'Signs in as' with nothing listed.

Pass, judged independently of the builder against the checkspace's travel blueprint, whose personas_from names acme-people, a blueprint that copy never registers; same unrecorded harness and ports as the other result (4713, 4725, 4749), with 4700 only read for the design and the as-built page. Every then step held. Opening travel.view.trip, the app's log is GET /dev/slow then GET /expenses/412, both with no uid, and the frame ends on the app's sign-in page, so the screen's own step and its path ran and no sign-in step did. While the step runs the card reads 'Setting up this screen: step 1 of 1', 'One of this screen's own steps.' and the note 'No sign-in ran. manager.view-only-team could not be read, because the blueprint acme-people is not registered on this machine. The rule says how to register it.' detail.signed-in reads 'manager.view-only-team could not be read, so nobody is signed in. Its personas are in the blueprint acme-people, which is not registered on this machine. Register it, then run the setup again.' with the command 'walkdown blueprints import <home of acme-people>', and the one list is headed 'This screen's own steps'. All of that is the accepted design's copy word for word, and the as-built page carries the same words over the example; both of its redlines are true (as designed, and drawn over the example with the unread user given to the payload). Run setup again asks the same two addresses and nothing else. The line stays whole and inside the window at 1000, 760 and 560 pixels wide. One edge, about 10% and reported to the dispatching agent rather than filed: the line's 'so nobody is signed in' is about what the panel ran, and after a manager screen of another blueprint in the same tab the app's cookie is still set, so the frame shows Expense 412 as 14 beside that line. Every as: screen of such a blueprint is unread, so the session can only come from another blueprint or from signing in by hand.
